mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months signals an impending monetary easing cycle, which reduces the risk-free rate and increases the present value of future equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in >60% of instances where FEDFUNDS declined for 3+ consecutive months, or Rank IC <0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 3.7% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in >60% of instances where UNRATE >3.7% for 2 consecutive months, or Rank IC <0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) over the past two months signals a broad-based demand contraction, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in >60% of instances where HOUST and RSAFS both declined for 2 consecutive months, or Rank IC <0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 104.0), a simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE > 3.6%) signals an imminent recession, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in >60% of instances where INDPRO <104.0 and UNRATE >3.6%, or Rank IC <0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the year-over-year CPI inflation rate above 3.0% signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in >60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY >3.0%, or Rank IC <0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the past 3 months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces consumer confidence and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in >60% of instances where PAYEMS declined for 3+ consecutive months, or Rank IC <0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) below 680,000 million dollars signals a contraction in consumer spending, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in >60% of instances where RSAFS <680000, or Rank IC <0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the past two months signals a supply shock and labor market stress, which increases corporate costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in >60% of instances where INDPRO declined and UNRATE rose for 2 consecutive months, or Rank IC <0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
